title: Production and purification of a soluble hydrogenase from Ralstonia eutropha H16 for potential hydrogen fuel cell applications
author: Jugder, Lebhar, et al.

An uptake hydrogenase activity (H2 oxidation) assay was developed based on previously described methods [2], [7], [10]. Further electrochemical studies were performed using cyclic voltammetry (CV) with the enzyme immobilized on modified EPG (edge plane pyrolytic graphite) electrodes. Differently modified electrodes with the SH protein film applied were employed to study H2 oxidizing activity. The preliminary results demonstrated that the enzyme exhibits H2 oxidation activity at the surface of electrode and therefore this enzyme is a promising candidate for biochemical oxidation in hydrogen biofuel cell research.

steps.title: Culture, harvest, and cell lysis
steps.instruction: Grow R. eutropha H16, harvest cells, and lyse them to obtain a cell‑free extract.

substeps.instruction: Pick a single colony from an FGN agar plate and inoculate 5 mL FGN medium in a 15 mL Falcon tube; incubate overnight at 30 °C on a shaker.
Transfer the overnight culture to a 1 L sterile baffled shake flask containing 100 mL FGN medium; grow overnight to generate the inoculum for the bioreactor.
Inoculate a laboratory‑scale glass bioreactor (working volume 5 L) with the pre‑culture; monitor growth by OD600 nm.
Operate the bioreactor at 30 °C, agitation 300–350 rpm, air flow 1–2 L min⁻¹; set initial pH 7.0–7.1 and maintain pH ≥6.4 by automatic addition of 1 M NaOH when needed.
At 15 h add FeCl₃ to a final concentration of 10 µM and NiCl₂ to 1 µM to maximise soluble hydrogenase (SH) activity.
After 48 h, harvest cells by centrifugation at 10 000 g, 4 °C for 10 min; wash pellets with 50 mM potassium phosphate (KPi) buffer, pH 7.0; store pellets at –80 °C.
Thaw pellets and resuspend in 50 mM KPi buffer containing cOmplete™ EDTA‑free protease inhibitor and DNase I (final 20 µg mL⁻¹); use a wet‑weight‑to‑buffer ratio of 1:5.
Sonicate the suspension with a Branson Digital Sonifier (1/8 tapered microtip) at 50 % amplitude; explore various duty cycles to optimise disruption.
Remove cell debris by centrifugation at 20 000 g for 50 min at 4 °C; keep the supernatant (cell‑free extract) on ice.

steps.title: Ammonium sulfate precipitation and chromatography
steps.instruction: Precipitate SH with ammonium sulfate and purify it using two anion‑exchange steps followed by size‑exclusion chromatography, all at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Add saturated ammonium sulfate to the cell‑free extract to reach 35 % (v/v) saturation; incubate on ice, then centrifuge at 10 000 g.
Increase the supernatant to 60 % saturation with ammonium sulfate; incubate on ice, centrifuge at 10 000 g, and dissolve the precipitated enzyme in 50 mM KPi buffer, pH 7.0.
Dialyse the dissolved protein twice for 3 h each against 2 L of 50 mM KPi buffer containing 1 mM EDTA (use Slide‑A‑Lyzer 10 K MWCO cassettes or SnakeSkin 10 K MWCO tubing).

First anion‑exchange (Q Sepharose FF 1 mL): equilibrate with 50 mM KPi, pH 7.0; elute with 1 M KCl, pH 6.5 using step gradients of 30 %, 43 % and 100 % of the 1 M KCl solution. For scale‑up, pack a 7.8 mL Q Sepharose FF column and apply a linear gradient 0–43 % B (≈0–430 mM KCl). Collect fractions, assay for SH activity, pool active fractions, and dialyse again against 2 L 50 mM KPi, pH 7.0 with 1 mM EDTA at 4 °C.

Second anion‑exchange (RESOURCE Q 1 mL, SOURCE™ 15Q medium): use the same buffer system and flow rate as above; apply a narrowed linear gradient 0–20 % B (0–200 mM KCl). Collect and assay fractions; pool those with highest activity.
Concentrate the pooled active fractions to ~0.5 mL using a Vivaspin® 20 10 K MWCO centrifugal concentrator.

Load the concentrate onto a Superdex 200 10/300 GL column (analytical grade) using a 500 µL sample loop; run with 50 mM KPi buffer containing 150 mM NaCl (ionic strength ≥20 mS cm⁻¹, conductivity ≈20 mS cm⁻¹) at 0.5 mL min⁻¹. Collect fractions, combine active ones, and reconcentrate.
Flush the final SH solution with nitrogen to remove headspace oxygen and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Mass spectrometric identification
steps.instruction: Confirm the identity of the purified SH by LC‑MS/MS analysis of tryptic peptides.

substeps.instruction: Excise the five protein bands (representing the six expected SH subunits) from a Coomassie‑stained SDS‑PAGE gel.

Digest each band with trypsin; load 2.5 µL of the digest onto an Ultimate 3000 HPLC system equipped with a 500 µm × 2 mm micro C18 pre‑column (Michrom) and a fritless nano‑C18 column (75 µm × ≈10 cm, 5 µm, 200 Å).
Desalt on the pre‑column with H₂O:CH₃CN (98:2, 0.05 % TFA) at 15 µL min⁻¹ for 4 min, then switch to the analytical column.
Elute peptides with a linear gradient from H₂O:CH₃CN (98:2, 0.1 % formic acid) to H₂O:CH₃CN (64:36, 0.1 % formic acid) at 250 nL min⁻¹ over 30 min.
Apply 2000 V to a low‑volume tee; position the column tip ~0.5 cm from the heated capillary (T = 280 °C) of an Orbitrap Velos mass spectrometer; acquire data in data‑dependent acquisition (DDA) mode.

Generate peak lists with Mascot Daemon/extract_msn and search using Mascot 2.2 (instrument type ESI‑TRAP, precursor tolerance 4 ppm, product tolerance ±0.4 Da). Specify variable modifications: acrylamide (C), oxidation (M), carbamidomethyl (C); enzyme specificity trypsin, allowing 1 missed cleavage.
Confirm that the identified peptides correspond to the hexameric SH of R. eutropha H16.

steps.title: In‑solution hydrogenase activity assay
steps.instruction: Measure H₂‑oxidizing activity of SH in solution using NAD⁺ as electron acceptor.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a septum‑sealed special optical glass cuvette; sparge with argon for 10 min (20 psi, 4–5 mL min⁻¹) then with H₂ for 10 min (same pressure and flow).
Add 100 µL SH solution to 2.9 mL reaction mixture containing 50 mM H₂‑saturated Tris/HCl buffer, pH 8.0, and 1 mM NAD⁺.
Pre‑incubate the mixture at 30 °C for 5 min in the Cary 100 UV–vis spectrophotometer (temperature controller).
Monitor NADH formation at 340 nm (ε = 6.22 mM⁻¹ cm⁻¹) by recording absorbance every 0.5 min for 10 min.
Calculate enzyme activity as µmol NAD⁺ reduced min⁻¹ using the slope (δA₃₄₀ nm min⁻¹) of the absorbance‑versus‑time plot.

steps.title: Electrochemical activity of immobilized hydrogenase
steps.instruction: Assess H₂‑oxidizing activity of SH immobilised on polymyxin‑modified EPG electrodes by cyclic voltammetry.

substeps.instruction: Modify edge‑plane pyrolytic graphite (EPG) electrodes with polymyxin to enable SH attachment.
Prepare 50 mM KPi buffer, pH 7.0; use a platinum wire as counter electrode and Ag/AgCl as reference; normalise potentials versus NHE.
Connect the electrode to an MPG‑2 potentiostat; set scan rate to 50 mV s⁻¹.
Add 5 µL of activated SH to the electrode surface; test both with and without polymyxin (no activity observed without polymyxin).
Equilibrate the cell with H₂‑saturated 50 mM KPi buffer (pH 7.0) and record cyclic voltammograms; apply a potential of –550 mV vs NHE and monitor current increase with incubation time.
Interpret the increase in H₂‑oxidation current as evidence of functional immobilised SH.
